stem:
Poonam will compute $18 \div 0.6$. Before calculating, she wants to predict how the quotient compares with the dividend $18$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The quotient is less than $18$ whenever a division is written, even for divisor $0.6$.
The divisor $0.6$ is produced by the dividend $18$, so the size comparison runs from quotient back to $0.6$.
Because the divisor $0.6$ is between $0$ and $1$, the quotient is greater than the dividend $18$.
The same size rule also settles the comparison when the divisor is negative.

teacher.key_rationale: For positive quantities, a divisor between 0 and 1 makes the quotient larger than the dividend (18÷0.6=30). Claiming the quotient is always smaller omits the divisor-size condition. Reversing divisor and dividend, or extending the rule to negative divisors, misses the hinge.
